'''Geoff Snider Miscommunication (tournament report)''' is the tournament report [[Geoff Snider]] posted on DeckTech on 7 March 2001 about [[2001 Normal DPC]].<ref name="tr-d1852">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2001-03-07-miscommunicationd1852/ miscommunication], DeckTech (Geoff "gsiva" Snider, 7 March 2001). Preservation copy: [https://stevetotheizz0.github.io/decktech_archives/reports/2001-03-07-miscommunicationd1852/ GitHub Pages].</ref> A short follow-up note by Geoff Snider to his report [[Geoff Snider Geoff's DPC Main Event (tournament report)]] on the [[2001 Normal DPC]]: he says he and his round-3 opponent [[Erik Petersen]] resolved his complaint about their slow, timed-out game right after the match, and apologizes for leaving that out of the report.

== Report info ==
* '''Author:''' [[Geoff Snider]] (byline: Geoff "gsiva" Snider)
* '''Published:''' 7 March 2001 (DeckTech)
* '''Report title:''' ''Miscommunication''
* '''Event:''' [[2001 Normal DPC]]
* '''Event date:''' 24 February 2001
* '''Site:''' Normal, Illinois

== Original report ==

'''miscommunication'''
* '''Author:''' Geoff "gsiva" Snider
* '''Published:''' Mar 7, 2001

<div style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family:inherit"><nowiki>
  miscommunication is something that plagues me constantly.



in my 3rd game of the DPC Normal, i played against Erik Petersen.  in my TR i addressed my disappointment in how long our game took.  Erik and i resolved that problem soon after our game.  i was not angry at him, for sometimes games do take time, but i was just angry at timing out.  it’s not his fault.  i hold no grudge.  i haven’t thought about since the DPC until it was brought to my attention tonight.



retracting what i stated (as the truth and as what i felt to be true during the game) would be inaccurate, or so i believe.



forgetting to include in my report that Erik and i communicated to each other post-match about my disappointment was my mistake.  the issue was resolved then and there, and i thank him for not allowing that wound to fester.



sometimes (okay...quite often) i’m a pretty bad sport if i feel i didn’t get a good game out of it.



hey, i apologize.  any comments?



(i’m probably leaving something out, but try not to crucify me for it....that’s the miscommunication talking again)
</nowiki></div>
